- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–7% to compensate for downward bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check sentiment for recent bullishness — if present, consider mean reversion bias and reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), sentiment may be bearish — consider upward adjustment and add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment turns neutral or positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price movements by 2–4 days; adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend direction, especially if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underperform; apply a 3–6% upward bias to forecast to counteract mean reversion bias.
